caption: Newanforbi v. Macomber
causes: Writ of Mandate (CCP §1085) — Compel ministerial duty to conduct individualized discharge determination
key_facts: Challenges the December 1, 2025 Discharge Review Report. CDCR abused discretion: facial scoring errors in Form 1502-DR, retaliatory input from compromised agents, wrong legal standard, blanket denial based on treatment non-completion. The report was authored November 14 and electronically approved November 19, 2025; December 1 is the form's printed Discharge Review Date used in the operative pleading.
procedural_status: Opening Brief filed. Hearing 03/27/2026 VACATED per Minute Order 03/10/2026 — service by mail insufficient; must serve per CCP §1096. Re-set: 05/29/2026, 11:00 a.m., Dept. 13A. Dept. 32 relocated to Dept. 13A effective 04/20/2026; Hon. Arguelles remains. Petition served on Jeffrey Macomber 04/13/2026 at 12:20 PM. AG filed Demurrer (CCP §430.10) on 05/04/2026 — argues other action pending (federal 2:25-cv-01460) and insufficient facts. Petitioner filed Opposition to Demurrer on 05/14/2026. AG (Kathleen R. Walton, DAG) filed Reply to Opposition on 05/18/2026 — three grounds: (1) no exhaustion of admin. remedies (Cal. Code Regs. tit. 15, §§3481, 3483, 3723); (2) habeas is a plain, speedy, adequate alternative remedy foreclosing mandamus (CCP §§1085–1086; Gilliam v. L.A. Municipal Court; In re Crow; In re Walters; In re Arias; CRC rule 4.551); (3) no ministerial duty under Pen. Code §3001 — 2017 offense under Pen. Code §3000(b)(2)(B) falls outside early-discharge review provisions; §§3008(d)(2) and 15 CCR §3574 govern treatment retention, not discharge review. AG seeks sustain without leave to amend. Tentative ruling: 05/28/2026 by 2:00 p.m. Demurrer Hearing: 05/29/2026, 11:00 a.m., Dept. 13A. | May 29, 2026 — Case closed. See Case Update (CU_26WM000028).
damages: Equitable: Vacate denial; order new review or discharge
